features.headline: Illinois' historic rout of Duke by the numbers
features.desc: Andrej Stojakovic's record 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium helped Illinois to a historic rout of Duke.
body: It has been a while since Duke lost at Cameron Indoor Stadium — since March 9, 2024, in fact — so when the second-longest home win streak in Division I is snapped, it's noticed.

No. 10 Illinois pulled off the 21-point rout of the No. 5 Blue Devils thanks to a historic performance by senior guard Andrej Stojakovic. His 46 points were the second most all time against Duke behind Penn's Ernie Beck in 1952 and the most by a visiting player to Cameron Indoor Stadium.
Let's dive into some of the numbers — courtesy of ESPN Research — behind Duke's worst home loss as an AP top-five team.
The Fighting Illini started three freshmen (Ethan Brown, Lincoln Williams and Quentin Coleman) in Tuesday's win.
They're the first team to win a road game against Duke with three freshmen in its starting lineup since North Carolina did it with Wayne Ellington, Ty Lawson and Brandan Wright on Feb. 7, 2007.

Andrej Stojakovic and Coleman together scored or assisted on 80 of Illinois' 99 points (81%). That's more points than Duke scored as a team (78). They scored 73 points together, the most by a duo against Duke in the past 30 years.

Stojakovic became the first player this decade and just the third player in the past 30 years to score at least 45 points in an AP Top 10 matchup, joining Kentucky's Malik Monk (47 against North Carolina in 2016) and Oklahoma's Buddy Hield (46 against Duke in 2016).
The 20 points Stojakovic scored before halftime were the most allowed by Duke since February 2021, when Notre Dame's Cormac Ryan put up 21.

features.headline: Irving, Walker III, Bowers and more Knockout league pickups for Week 11
features.desc: As the number of teams shrink, the number of stars available in Knockout leagues grows. Here are the ones to get.
body: Lady Luck's influence on Knockout leagues is growing ever greater.

Bad fortune in the injury department spawned the largest knockout rate by any individual player all season in Week 10. Drake Maye's likely season-ending fractured ankle not only set back his New England Patriots' playoff chances, but also eliminated his Knockout teams in 21.7% of leagues.

Brock Bowers' own ankle injury landed him high on the list, as he played only 19% of the Las Vegas Raiders' snaps, scored a season-low 3.8 fantasy points and was on knocked-out teams in 13.1% of leagues.
Fellow tight end Travis Kelce, who battled ankle and calf issues in what was a 5.0-fantasy-point Week 10, was on knocked-out teams in 12.0% of leagues.
Meanwhile, Kenneth Walker III and Puka Nacua, both ruled out in advance of their games, had 16.3% and 12.8% knockout rates.

But it's not only injuries that prove problematic at this midseason stage of Knockout leagues. Unfortunate outcomes, especially those in what were favorable matchups on paper, prove comparably devastating.
Chris Olave scored 6.0 fantasy points and had a 13.1% knockout rate, while his WR1 counterpart from that same game, Tetairoa McMillan, scored 6.5 points and was knocked out in 12.2% of leagues.
Jonathan Taylor scored 12.3 points and had a 12.2% knockout rate.
It's fantasy football, and anything can happen. But that doesn't mean we should adopt a throw-up-our-hands, aw-shucks type of approach.
Rather, the increasingly devastating effects of such unexpected bad outcomes reminds us of two critical Knockout strategies as we progress through the season's second half:

features.headline: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
features.desc: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."
body: CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Chuba Hubbard knows that no one is perfect. But that hasn't stopped the Carolina Panthers' running back from chasing perfection.

And after a forgettable, injury-marred 2025 campaign, during which he lost his starting job after a career season in 2024, the team captain is leading the backfield again, and he's perhaps better than ever.

"I pride myself in hard work and staying consistent in knowing what I can do and trying to bring my best every single day, so it's more so just fighting for excellence and fighting to be perfect in every way possible," Hubbard told ESPN.
Hubbard, 27, signed a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension during his breakout 2024 campaign, when he rushed for 1,195 yards and produced 11 total touchdowns in 15 games.

Through eight games in 2026, he has rushed for 619 yards and produced seven total touchdowns, bouncing back as the Panthers have struggled to find consistency almost everywhere else during a three-game losing streak and a 3-5 start.
But those numbers don't tell the complete story of Hubbard's value. He's talented, sure, but his true worth is as a tone-setter for the organization.

Though he was selected by the franchise, while Matt Rhule was the coach, in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL draft, Hubbard has established himself as the standard-bearer for the Dave Canales era over the past three seasons.
And with Carolina fighting to maintain its position atop the NFC South, his value has become apparent, if not paramount, to the team's ability to recalibrate its season.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
The deal: Three years, $52.5 million Grade: D+

We've had two significant signings off the free agent market so far, and both involve freshly minted ex-Milwaukee Brewers: After Jake Bauers landed with the Boston Red Sox on Friday, the Chicago White Sox plucked Dustin May off the championship Milwaukee pitching staff.

Whereas Boston was banking on Bauers' 2026 breakout being his current true talent level, the White Sox are perhaps taking a bigger gamble that May's past five years do not represent his real level of ability.
Since his early shine as a top Los Angeles Dodgers prospect, which included some promising early work in the majors, May's career has been journeyman-like.
Around injuries that cost him the 2024 season, he has put up 0.9 bWAR with a 91 ERA+ over 356 big-league innings for the period covering 2022 through last season.
May became a fallback addition for the Brewers at the 2026 trade deadline after more glitzy pursuits (ahem, Tarik Skubal) fell short.

features.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Joe Burrow takes QB lead, Chuba Hubbard continues rise
features.desc: Need to make or assess a trade offer? With six teams on their bye week, these rankings are designed to help.
body: Move over, Josh Allen; there's a new top fantasy QB in town, and he plays for the Cincinnati Bengals.

There's a lot of movement at running back with Chuba Hubbard, Blake Corum and Tony Pollard earning more confidence from managers, and the early returns on Justin Jefferson's reunion with Kirk Cousins has him moving up the board.

Here is my latest fantasy football rankings update for the rest of the season by position to help you identify trade values and long-term adds and drops. You'll find the top 100 at the bottom of this column.

Rankings changes: Joe Burrow and his managers are enjoying a historic run as he has accounted for four or more touchdowns in five consecutive games and scored at least 28 fantasy points in four straight.

With a friendly schedule the rest of the way, Burrow passes Josh Allen for the top spot in the rankings. The other big move is Drake Maye (ankle) leaving the top 10 as Tommy DeVito subs for him. Sad emoji.
Later, Deshaun Watson, Jacoby Brissett and Cam Ward move up to QB2 range.

Rankings changes: No, Christian McCaffrey does not usurp the top spot after his 46.3-point outing in Week 10 (Jahmyr Gibbs scored 44.2 points!), but he does move to No. 3, sliding past Bijan Robinson, who has reached 18 points in one of the past six games and remains in the top five.

Jonathan Taylor leaves the top five. Chuba Hubbard continues his rise, as do Blake Corum and Tony Pollard in RB2 territory. Emmett Johnson becomes a solid flex option, while Seth McGowan and Kaelon Black are close. Welcome back, Omarion Hampton.
